Sibling of blocking 3 (rule 8): packages/platform/src/shell.ts run() spawns without detached, so killTree's process.kill(-pid) fails with ESRCH and only the direct child is killed (child.kill). Every command the process sandbox stops or times out leaves its grandchildren running on Linux and macOS: `npm test` with its node test runner, a CLI try that spawns a child, a worker's long command. Windows is not affected (taskkill /T). Evidence: the reviewer's probe-abort and this fixup's try-run.test.ts 'out of time' case on the fixer's head ('still running 10 s after the try ran out of time: <pids>'). Fixing it needs detached process groups for sandboxed runs (or a guard like the server driver's), with tests for git and npm.

The process sandbox's 'network off' is only HTTP(S)_PROXY pointing at a deny-all EgressProxy (sandbox/process.ts, egress-proxy.ts envFor). Node 22's http and fetch ignore those variables, so a tool or a worker's command can reach the network. The try evidence, the user guide and ADR 0110 now say so. Other texts that promise the process sandbox has no network (if any outside this area) should be checked.
